maintained_repo_url: N/A (single research repo, last pushed 2024-09-10; no continuously-maintained leaderboard or paper-list).
task_domain: Decision-making / embodied-style interactive text-game agents (planning, exploration, navigation in partially observable text worlds) as the primary domain, plus a secondary static multi-hop QA evaluation. Environments: TextWorld text games (Treasure Hunt, Cleaning, Cooking) and NetHack (roguelike); QA on MuSiQue and HotpotQA.
problem_setting: Interactive, online, SINGLE-agent setting. An LLM agent (Ariadne) interacts step-by-step with an unknown Partially Observable MDP (POMDP) text environment: at each step t it receives observation o_t and emits action a_t; environment rewards r_t are used only for evaluation and are NOT visible to the agent (no gradient updates, no RL training of the LLM, frozen GPT-4-0125-preview backbone). There is no offline corpus and no ground-truth world graph given; the agent must learn a structured world model from scratch via interaction by extracting triplets from textual observations and writing them into a growing memory graph. The agent must remember long-horizon information, filter outdated facts, navigate and explore. A separate, simpler decoupled study compares against RL baselines (GATA, LTL-GATA, EXPLORER) on a 4-level Cooking variant from Adhikari et al. 2021, and a third static multi-hop QA study (MuSiQue / HotpotQA) treats document context as the source over which the same memory graph is built (here non-interactive, offline corpus).
what_is_retrieved: experiences/knowledge from the agent's own learned memory graph: (1) semantic triplets / semantic edges (object1, relation, object2) representing the current structured world state, and (2) episodic vertices, i.e. full past textual observations o_t (and the episodic edges linking observations to the triplets extracted at that step). In the QA setting the same units are retrieved from a graph built over the document(s).
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent itself writes (HYBRID semantic+episodic), constructed online during interaction. For the interactive games the memory graph is built entirely from the agent's own observations (no static external KB/corpus/API). For the auxiliary multi-hop QA the same AriGraph is built over the provided document(s) before answering, so that sub-setting grounds on a (per-query) constructed graph rather than the agent's evolving experience.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Top-k retrieval with two coupled stages but no learned ranking metric: SemanticSearch returns up to width-w edges per BFS hop within depth d (a variable-size relevant subgraph), and EpisodicSearch returns the k most relevant episodic vertices (k fixed). The objective is to surface the relevant subgraph + most-relevant past observations to support decision-making, not a fixed top-k ranking optimized to Recall@k/nDCG, and not an explicit minimal-complete-set objective; effective size is driven by graph connectivity and the d/w/k hyperparameters.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: partial, Revise: yes (of the world model, not of cases), Retain: yes]. AriGraph Retrieves relevant triplets+observations, Retains every new triplet and observation, and Revises stored knowledge by detecting and removing outdated/conflicting triplets when the world changes. 'Reuse' is partial: retrieved knowledge is fed to planning/decision-making as context rather than reusing a prior solution case. (Approximate mapping; the work is NOT framed as CBR.)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner. It is framed as a knowledge-graph world model integrating semantic and episodic memory for LLM agents.
retrieval_unit: Two unit types from a knowledge graph: (a) KG-subgraph / semantic edge = a single semantic triplet (object1, relation, object2); and (b) episodic vertex = a full past textual observation o_t. Episodic edges (temporal 'happened at the same time' links) connect each observation vertex to the triplets extracted at that step. Retrieval returns a relevant set of triplets (the subgraph) plus the top-k episodic observations.
index_source: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced. In the interactive games the AriGraph world model is constructed and continuously updated from scratch during the agent's interaction (each observation adds an episodic vertex/edge and triggers triplet extraction + outdated-triplet removal). In the QA setting the graph is induced from the supplied documents prior to answering. No pre-existing static KB is used.
index_structure_topology: Knowledge GRAPH (dependency/semantic graph) augmented with an episodic layer: semantic vertices (objects) connected by semantic edges (triplets), plus episodic vertices (observations) connected to their triplets via episodic edges ('hyper-relational'/temporal links). Spatial relations (e.g. 'hall, east of, kitchen', 'kitchen, has an unexplored exit, south') are stored as triplets enabling graph-based navigation/route inference. Edge text is embedded for similarity search. This is a structured graph index, contrasted with flat unstructured vector RAG.
retriever_type: Hybrid graph-traversal + dense retrieval. A BFS-like Memory Graph Search (Algorithm 1/2): at each hop EmbedAndRetrieve uses a pretrained dense encoder (Contriever for games; BGE-M3 for QA) to embed edges and the query and return the top-w edges by dot-product similarity, expanding to incident vertices up to depth d; episodic search then scores episodic vertices by how many retrieved triplets they contain. No trained/learned retriever, no BM25, no LLM-as-retriever, no reranker stage.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf encoders, hand-designed scoring). Semantic relevance uses frozen pretrained Contriever (games) / BGE-M3 (QA) embeddings with dot-product similarity; the episodic relevance score is a hand-crafted formula rel(v_e^i) = (n_i / max(N_i,1)) * log2(max(N_i,1)) where n_i is the number of retrieved input triplets associated with episodic vertex i and N_i is the total triplets incident, with log weighting (single-triplet observations assigned zero weight). No contrastive fine-tuning, LM-feedback, RL, or downstream-effectiveness training of the retriever.
query_construction: Query is formed from the agent's current situation. For semantic search the query set Q is derived from the current observation/state (and relevant entities); during graph traversal each newly reached semantic vertex serves as a sub-query for the next EmbedAndRetrieve hop (multi-hop query expansion across the graph). For QA, the question (decomposed into the entities/relations needed) drives the multi-hop semantic search. Episodic search uses the retrieved triplets as its query into the episodic layer.
query_granularity: Step/state-level (a fresh retrieval is performed at each interaction step before planning/decision-making), with an internal multi-hop, two-level structure: semantic search (BFS over triplets, depth d / width w) followed by episodic search (top-k observations). For QA it is task-level per question but still internally multi-hop.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / per-step. Retrieval into working memory occurs at every environment step (each new observation triggers world-model update then retrieval of relevant semantic subgraph + top-k episodic memories). Internally it is a multi-hop BFS rather than a single one-shot lookup. Not uncertainty-triggered or routed by a learned classifier.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (per-step / event-driven): every observation triggers (i) a world-model update and (ii) retrieval to repopulate working memory before planning and decision-making. An auxiliary 'exploration check' LLM prompt decides whether the current plan needs exploration (activating unexplored-exit detection that adds candidate exits to working memory), but this gates exploration mode rather than gating whether retrieval happens. No token-confidence, attention-uncertainty, reflection-token, or learned-complexity trigger.
reranking: No dedicated second-stage reranker (no cross-encoder / RRF / instruction-tuned reranker). Ranking is the single similarity score (dot product) within the BFS for semantic edges, and the hand-crafted relevance formula for episodic vertices; top-w / top-k are taken directly.
retrieved_context_refinement: Light structural selection rather than learned refinement: the BFS bounds the retrieved subgraph by depth d and width w; the episodic relevance formula down-weights low-information (single-triplet) observations; the retrieved semantic subgraph and top-k episodic observations are then placed into working memory. Outdated/conflicting triplets are removed at write time (world-model update) rather than as post-retrieval filtering. No reason-in-documents distillation or learned compression of retrieved text.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/APIs are indexed; the store holds learned semantic triplets and raw observations, not tool/skill documentation).
index_content_separation: Partial/implicit: semantic edges (compact triplets) act as the lightweight retrievable keys and are embedded for search, while each episodic vertex stores the full observation text loaded into the prompt only when its observation is among the retrieved top-k. There is no explicit progressive-disclosure SOP-index-then-content protocol; it is the two-layer semantic(compact)/episodic(full-text) design.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (not a tool-retrieval system; no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling tool registry or CRUD auto-sync). The 'dynamic' aspect is that the knowledge graph is continuously updated (insert new triplets, delete outdated ones, append episodic vertices) during interaction.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools/APIs; no inter-tool dependency modeling). Spatial/relational dependencies between locations and objects are modeled in the KG for navigation, but this is environment-state structure, not tool dependency.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation. The retrieved relevant semantic subgraph and top-k episodic observations are written into the agent's working memory (alongside goal, current observation, recent history, current plan, and unexplored exits) and injected as text into the planning prompt and the ReAct decision-making prompt, grounding plan generation/update and action selection. No training signal or latent-token injection; the frozen LLM consumes retrieved knowledge as text.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan-then-act per step within an interaction loop. Pipeline at each step: update AriGraph -> retrieve semantic+episodic knowledge into working memory -> Planning module creates/updates a plan as task-relevant sub-goals (each with a reason), also evaluating outcomes of the previous action and adjusting the plan -> ReAct-based Decision-making module reads working memory and selects one valid action (articulating rationale first). Planning is separated from decision-making. A graph-specific 'go to location' macro-action lets the agent infer optimal routes from stored spatial triplets. No MCTS/tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-step within the rollout (per environment step): retrieval, planning update, and decision-making are interleaved once per action over the long-horizon trajectory (max 60 steps Cooking, 150 steps other games). Within a single retrieval, traversal is multi-hop over the graph. Not per-CoT-token.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A for classic CBR case adaptation. Retrieved knowledge is used as in-context evidence; the LLM synthesizes plans/actions from it. The closest analog is execution-feedback-driven REVISION of the world model itself (outdated triplets detected and replaced as the environment changes), not adaptation of a retrieved solution case.
retrieved_item_representation: Structured natural-language: semantic triplets (object1, relation, object2) rendered as text form the relevant subgraph, and full raw observation texts form the episodic items; both injected as text into working-memory prompt fields. No executable program/skill or latent/soft tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Mixed: distilled structured facts (semantic triplets = compact state knowledge, a structured-note-like abstraction) coexisting with raw low-abstraction episodic observations (full past observation text). Spatial-relation triplets additionally serve a procedural/navigation role.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Several heuristic guards: (1) write-time outdated-triplet detection-and-removal keeps the semantic graph consistent with the changing world (a carefully prompted, conservative replacement rule that errs toward retaining facts); (2) the episodic relevance log-weighting assigns zero weight to single-triplet (low-information) observations to suppress distractors; (3) bounded BFS depth d / width w limits retrieval of irrelevant graph regions. No retriever-aware training, learned relevance evaluator, or self-reflection filter.
memory_type: graph memory integrating semantic memory (knowledge-graph triplets) and episodic memory (per-step observation vertices) within one memory-graph framework; long-term, persistent, single-agent, online-updated. The authors explicitly note procedural memory is left to future work.
write_back: True. Every observation is written back: a new episodic vertex (full observation) and episodic edges are added, new semantic triplets extracted from the observation are inserted, and outdated/conflicting triplets are removed. The graph is the agent's learned world model.
online_growth: Yes. The memory graph is built from scratch and grows/updates continuously during interaction at test time. Authors report growth saturates as the agent becomes familiar with the environment, and grows moderately for larger/harder environments; higher-quality LLM backbones produce slower graph growth (cleaner extraction).
write_back_trigger: Per-step (every observation). Each environment step triggers a world-model update: append episodic vertex/edges, insert new semantic triplets, and detect+remove outdated triplets. Writes are NOT conditioned on task success/failure (no reward signal is used for writing). (The Reflexion BASELINE, by contrast, writes reflective notes on failure across trials, but that is a comparison method, not AriGraph.)
failure_experience_usage: No explicit success/failure labeling in AriGraph itself: the agent stores all observations and the current factual world state regardless of outcome; there is no failure-only corrective-rule store or success-vs-failure contrastive retrieval. (Reflexion, used only as a baseline, performs cross-trial failure reflection; AriGraph operates within a single trajectory and updates state, not failure rules.)
memory_evolution_update: Both append and mutate: episodic memory is append-only (new observation vertices/edges); semantic memory is dynamically mutated via delta-update / refine-overwrite, i.e. new triplets are inserted and outdated or conflicting incident triplets are detected (compared against new triplets) and deleted/replaced when the world state changes (e.g. 'item, is in, locker' -> 'item, is in, inventory'). Link-and-evolve via episodic edges connecting observations to triplets.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/case-selection is a fixed graph-search + frozen-embedding similarity procedure with hand-crafted episodic scoring; it is not an RL/learned policy (no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, or trained retrieval policy). The agent's action policy is the frozen LLM with ReAct; only the world model (not the retriever) is 'learned' (constructed) online.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory: one Ariadne agent builds and uses its own AriGraph. No cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: (1) Custom TextWorld text games in three families with difficulty tiers: Treasure Hunt (Medium 12 rooms/4 keys, Hard 16 rooms/5 keys, Hardest 36 rooms/7 keys + distractors), Cleaning (9 rooms, 11 misplaced items), Cooking (Medium 9 locations/3 ingredients, Hard 12 locations/4 ingredients, Hardest adds closed doors + inventory management); (2) a 4-level Cooking variant from Adhikari et al. 2021 for RL comparison; (3) NetHack (roguelike, via NetPlay) with Room-Obs vs Level-Obs settings; (4) static multi-hop QA: MuSiQue and HotpotQA (200 random samples each, following GraphReader/Li et al. 2024a). LLM backbone gpt-4-0125-preview for games; GPT-4 and GPT-4o-mini for QA.
benchmark_family: Embodied/interactive text-game decision-making (TextWorld; closest to ALFWorld/ScienceWorld family) and roguelike (NetHack) for the primary tasks; multi-hop QA (MuSiQue, HotpotQA) for the secondary evaluation. Spans decision-making/RL-comparison and multi-hop QA families.
baselines: Interactive text games (all sharing Ariadne's identical planning+decision modules, varying ONLY the memory module): Full History, Summarization, standard RAG (top-k vector retrieval), Simulacra (Generative Agents memory; recency+importance+relevance scoring with reflection), Reflexion (cross-trial verbal reflection). RL baselines on the Cooking-variant: GATA, LTL-GATA, EXPLORER (best reported numbers from Adhikari et al. 2021, Tuli et al. 2022, Basu et al. 2024); plus GPT-4 Full-History. Human players (Top-3 and All). NetHack: NetPlay [Room obs], NetPlay [Level obs] (memory-oracle). Multi-hop QA: BM25(top-3), Ada-002(top-3), GPT-4 full context, GPT-4 + supporting facts, ReadAgent(GPT-4), GraphReader(GPT-4), HOLMES(GPT-4), GraphRAG(GPT-4o-mini).
key_metrics: Text games: normalized game score (relative to max attainable points; 1.0 = task solved), reported as average of the top-3 of 5 runs, with step caps (60 Cooking, 150 others). NetHack: Score and number of dungeon Levels reached. Multi-hop QA: Exact Match (EM) and F1. Efficiency: prompt/completion token usage per step (games) and per task (QA), and cost ratio vs GraphRAG.
headline_result: On the interactive text games the Ariadne agent with AriGraph markedly outperforms all memory baselines and scales to harder environments, reaching near-human performance: normalized scores of 1.0 on Treasure Hunt (all three difficulties), 1.0 on Cooking (Medium and Hard), 0.65 on Cooking Hardest, and 0.79 on Cleaning, vs. e.g. RAG (0.33 Treasure Hunt / 0.36 Cooking / 0.39 Cleaning) and Full History (0.47-0.49 / 0.18 / 0.05). It also beats RL agents (GATA, LTL-GATA, EXPLORER) on all 4 Cooking difficulty levels. On NetHack, Ariadne [Room obs] scores 593.0+/-202.6 (6.33 levels), comparable to the memory-oracle NetPlay [Level obs] 675.3+/-130.3 (7.33 levels) and far above NetPlay [Room obs] 341.7+/-109.1 (3.67 levels). On multi-hop QA (v3 Table 2), AriGraph(GPT-4) reaches 68.0 EM / 74.7 F1 on HotpotQA and 45.0 EM / 57.0 F1 on MuSiQue, competitive with HOLMES(GPT-4) (66.0/78.0 HotpotQA; 48.0/58.0 MuSiQue) and >10x cheaper than GraphRAG.
ablations: Key ablations (Table 4 normalized scores): 'AriGraph w/o episodic' (semantic graph only) drops on tasks needing detailed recall: Cooking 1.0 -> 0.64 (Medium) and 1.0 -> 0.45 (Hard), Treasure Hunt Hard 1.0 -> 0.67, while it slightly IMPROVES Cleaning (0.79 -> 0.92, where filtering outdated location info matters more than long-term recall), showing episodic memory is critical for recall-heavy tasks and less so for state-filtering tasks. 'AriGraph w/o exploration' (no graph-based unexplored-exit detection / go-to macro) drops Treasure Hunt 1.0 -> 0.87 and Cooking 1.0 -> 0.87. Backbone ablation: 'AriGraph LLaMA-3-70B' is much weaker (Treasure Hunt 0.47, Cooking 0.67, Cleaning 0.5) than GPT-4, showing dependence on backbone extraction quality. NetHack ablation shows Room-Obs+AriGraph matches the Level-Obs oracle. QA: replacing Contriever with BGE-M3 for text encoding.
evaluation_decoupling: Partial. Intrinsic retrieval ranking metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are NOT reported; the authors explicitly state they do not measure graph correctness against a 'true graph' (too variable), instead reporting graph growth-rate and update-rate as process diagnostics. End-to-end metrics (game score, NetHack score/levels, QA EM/F1) are the main signals; the RL-comparison and NetHack-oracle studies decouple memory contribution from the decision module.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Outcome metrics dominate (normalized game score, NetHack score/levels, QA EM/F1), but process-level diagnostics are reported: per-step performance dynamics (Appendix G), graph growth-rate and update-rate over time (Fig.5/6, incl. a random-walk construction experiment), and component ablations isolating semantic vs. episodic memory and exploration.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported (Table 3). Text games per-step token usage: Ariadne ~6,000 prompt / 500 completion tokens, vs RAG 4,000/350, Summary 3,800/350, Full History (step 150) 14,000/350, Simulacra 7,500/400, Reflexion 5,800/350 — i.e. AriGraph is far cheaper than Full History and avoids its blow-up, while richer than plain RAG. QA per-task: AriGraph 11,000 prompt / 2,500 completion vs GraphRAG 115,000 / 20,000 — AriGraph is >10x cheaper than GraphRAG at competitive accuracy.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Budget controlled by graph-search hyperparameters: SemanticSearch returns up to width w edges per BFS hop bounded by depth d; EpisodicSearch returns the top-k episodic observations (k fixed per run); working memory also holds n_prev recent observation/action pairs, the goal, current observation, plan, and unexplored exits. Selection is similarity-then-truncate within the d/w/k budget (no adaptive precision-driven k). Net per-step prompt ~6,000 tokens.
benchmark_construction_and_size: TextWorld games are custom-authored (Inform 7 / TextWorld) with explicit difficulty tiers (Treasure Hunt 12/16/36 rooms; Cleaning 9 rooms/11 misplaced items; Cooking 9-12 locations/3-4 ingredients + Hardest with closed doors); scoring is rule-verifiable (points per key/item/recipe step). NetHack via NetPlay. QA uses 200 random samples each from MuSiQue and HotpotQA (existing datasets, answer-verifiable EM/F1). Five runs per game with top-3 averaged; difficulty signaled by baseline failure (baselines cannot find the 2nd key on Treasure Hunt Hardest).
builds_on: TextWorld text-game framework (Cote et al. 2018); NetHack Learning Environment (Kuttler et al. 2020) via NetPlay (Jeurissen et al. 2024); ReAct (Yao et al. 2023) for decision-making; Generative Agents/Simulacra (Park et al. 2023) and Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) as memory baselines/inspiration; Contriever (Izacard et al. 2022) and BGE-M3 (Chen et al. 2024) dense encoders; cognitive-science semantic/episodic memory distinction; KG-from-text QA line (GraphReader/Li et al. 2024a, HOLMES, GraphRAG, HippoRAG, ReadAgent); RL text-game world-model line (GATA / Adhikari et al. 2021, LTL-GATA / Tuli et al. 2022, EXPLORER / Basu et al. 2024); cognitive architectures for language agents (Sumers et al. 2024).
contrasts_with: Unstructured LLM-agent memory: Full History (costly, context-limited), Summarization (lossy), plain vector RAG (scattered/unstructured retrieval), Simulacra/Generative-Agents recency-importance-relevance memory, and Reflexion cross-trial reflection — all of which lack structured semantic+episodic graph state and dynamic updating. Skill-library/episodic agents (Voyager, Ghost-in-the-Minecraft, Jarvis-1) that lack semantic graph structure and rely on external game knowledge. KG-QA methods (GraphReader, HOLMES, GraphRAG, HippoRAG) that build static document KGs but do NOT support updates in dynamic interactive environments. RL world-model agents (GATA, LTL-GATA, EXPLORER) that require training.
lineage: Group F (decision-making / memory / RL): a knowledge-graph world-model + episodic-memory architecture for online experience-based LLM agents in interactive POMDP text games. Extends the episodic memory-stream lineage (Generative Agents/Reflexion) by adding a dynamically-updated semantic knowledge graph and graph-traversal retrieval, and connects it to the KG-from-text QA lineage (GraphRAG/HOLMES/GraphReader). Sits upstream of later structured-memory / graph-memory agent frameworks; positioned as learning a structured world model from scratch via interaction.
